messages:
marta: Heads up — sketching a per-tenant routing policy matrix for free/pro/enterprise + region. Posting a small proposal below; want to lock enforcement semantics before we wire the console.
ryan: quick q — should free tier be strictly pinned to low-cost variants, or can we allow occasional premium fallbacks (metered) when spare capacity exists?
kim: +1 to configurable behavior. My take: soft enforcement for free (allow fallbacks but tag/meter), hard enforcement for enterprise only when in contract. Pro tier maybe a hybrid.
devex-sam: Console UX constraints: we need an explicit "allow_fallbacks" toggle per policy, plus a tooltip showing sample cost delta and expected latency. Also: preview modal for rollout impact.
marta: Here's a minimal policy shape I sketched for the policy engine (pseudo-JSON):
```
{
  "tenant": "acme-corp",
  "policies": [
    {
      "region": "us-west",
      "tier": "free",
      "preferred_variants": ["redwood-small-int8"],
      "fallback_variants": ["redwood-tiny-int8","redwood-small-fp16"],
      "quota": {"daily_tokens": "50000", "burst_tokens": "1000", "enforce": "soft"}
    },
    {
      "region": "eu-central",
      "tier": "enterprise",
      "preferred_variants": ["redwood-pro-fp16"],
      "fallback_variants": [],
      "quota": {"daily_tokens": "unlimited", "enforce": "hard"}
    }
  ]
}
```
marta: The important enforcement semantics to decide: 'soft' = allow routing to fallback but tag & bill at MSRP difference + emit "fallback_event" telemetry; 'hard' = return 429 or route to a compatible variant only if explicit allow flag is set.
ryan: operational question — where do we enforce quota? API gateway (fast reject) or routing layer (more context, can do smart fallback and KV cache)? My vote: gateway for hard rejects, routing layer for soft enforcement so we can choose cheaper variant transparently.
kim: agree. Also need to think about rate-limits vs token-quotas. Burst semantics matter for chat workloads. If we do soft enforcement in the routing layer we must push a clear telemetry flag so billing/service owners can backfill adjustments.
devex-sam: For Console -> UX, propose three columns in the tenant policy editor: Policy | Fallback behavior (allow/soft/hard) | Expected delta (tokens/cost). Add an "Audit Preview" button that simulates 24h for sample prompts.
marta: rollout plan idea — start with opt-in per-tenant flag for "allow_fallbacks_preview=v1" and capture rollup metrics for 72h. If metrics look sane, flip default for free tier.
ryan: can we add a feature flag per-region? Some customers (regulated) should never fallback across regions.
kim: yes, policy supports region scoping (see sketch). We should also surface a per-tenant whitelist of allowed fallback variants for compliance.
marta: telemetry events we need: fallback_decision {tenant, request_id, from_variant, to_variant, reason, cost_delta}, quota_violation {tenant, type, token_over}, quota_enforcement_action.
ryan: and tie those into the Console usage dashboard with sampling so we don't blow retention costs.
ops-bot: deploy triggered by @marta:policy-proposal -> staging/policy-engine v0.9.3
marta: Cool, next steps: @kim can you write a short RFC paragraph about "soft vs hard" semantics? @devex-sam can you mock the Console panel with the three-column layout? I'll spin up a staging flag and add telemetry hooks.
kim: will do, drafting now.
devex-sam: I'll do a quick Figma and link it in this thread later. :thumbsup:
marta: Thanks all — noting action items and will follow up with a short RFC in #eng-platform-rfcs.
